statements.t: The Company strives to position itself as an energy-systems platform for “physical AI,” prioritizing product revenue growth, gross margin improvement, and cost discipline across its target markets, which include space and defense, the low-altitude drone economy, AI data center backup power, Energy-as-a-Service for critical infrastructure, and robotics.
We expect to use the remaining proceeds to fund our planned operations and growth initiatives.
The Company expects to generate approximately $4 million in annualized cost savings upon full implementation.

The Company expects to incur severance and related costs ranging from $0.35 million to $0.65 million in connection with the reduction, substantially all of which will be recognized in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Through our KULR ONE battery platform, we design and manufacture high-power battery systems, and in 2027 we intend to focus our product development and commercial resources on two markets: autonomous systems and power infrastructure.

We will continue to serve select existing space and defense customers with our KULR ONE Space products and custom battery assemblies, while concentrating new program activity on the autonomous systems and power infrastructure markets described above.

To that end, we have established partnerships with battery cell manufacturers to source cells intended to meet these requirements, we have invested in the development of our own battery management systems (“BMS”) and battery chargers so that the electronics in a KULR ONE battery system are designed and sourced under our control, and we perform final assembly, testing and certification.

Applicable standards, including UN 38.3, IEC 62133 and UL 2580, are encoded as design rules that are checked on every build; these rules support, but do not replace, physical testing, customer qualification and first-article builds, and the Company's engineering release and quality processes will be unchanged.

We believe that owning this platform, rather than licensing multiple third-party systems, gives us greater control over our data, lets us adapt workflows quickly as the business changes, and may reduce software licensing and integration costs over time.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, the gross loss margin on contract services increased compared to the prior year period, driven primarily by lower contract services revenue, a gross loss on the battery management system development program for our largest contract services customer due to excess labor and material costs, and labor costs for rework and follow-on support provided to customers on…
We expect that our non-reimbursable R&D expenses will decrease beginning in the fourth quarter of 2026 and further in 2027.
Our BMS and charger development programs are expected to be completed in early 2027, after which the related third-party engineering costs will not recur.

We have also deployed KULR ONE Studio Designer Pro, an AI-based engineering design tool trained on our proprietary intellectual property, including more than 900 battery pack designs on file ranging from 1S to 72S configurations and characterization data for 34 cell types from nine cell vendors; we expect the tool, which is an all in one AI driven CAE and CAD platform, to reduce the engineering hours and outside…

In addition, during the fourth quarter of 2026 we implemented a reduction in force intended to streamline our development process, lower our cost structure, shorten turnaround time on customer programs and concentrate our engineering resources on our strategic customer accounts.

Although we expect to incur severance and related costs ranging from $0.35 million to $0.65 million in connection with the reduction, we expect to generate approximately $4 million in annualized cost savings upon full implementation.

The amount and timing of any decrease will depend on the number and complexity of R&D programs, the pace of qualification activities and the extent to which our design tools deliver the expected productivity improvements.
We do not expect to incur further costs related to our former Bitcoin mining business.
We do not intend to acquire or hold BTC or other digital assets as treasury reserve assets in the future.
To the extent that there are material differences between these estimates and actual results, our financial results will be affected.

statements.t: The Company expects R&D expenses to decrease beginning in the fourth quarter of 2026 and further in 2027, as the production line bring-up and the new pack development programs are completed in the fourth quarter and the battery management system and charger programs are completed in early 2027.

In 2026, KULR built a supply chain intended to meet those requirements: partnerships with battery cell manufacturers for compliant cells, its own battery management systems and chargers so that the electronics in KULR ONE Air batteries are designed and sourced under KULR’s control, and in-house final assembly, testing and certification at its new production line facility (“Forge 2”).
The Company expects these actions to generate approximately $4 million in annualized cost savings upon full implementation.

The Company expects to incur severance and related costs ranging from $0.35 million to $0.65 million in connection with the reduction, substantially all of which will be recognized in the fourth quarter of 2026.
